questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have travelled to Scotland before and loved the mix of beautiful nature and citylife which made me choose Glasgow. In addition to this, going to an English-speaking country seemed to make it easiest for me socially. I was also aware that this was my last chance to do an exchange to the UK through the Erasmus+ programme because of Brexit.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would have loved to have met more Scottish people at the university. I'm not rating it a 10 because I also found that it was significant difficult for exchange students to find accommodation, something that impacted both mine and others experience negatively. The process of getting courses was very confusing as well, resulting in me not getting the courses that I hoped to.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. Mostly from my sending institution. The receiving institution didn't offer much information about process of application for courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The visiting team was a great help with any uncertainties I had. Overall, the communication with the institutions was fine, but not having ever been on exchange before it can be hard to know what exactly to ask when you yourself have to seek the information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Again, the visiting team was great in assisting me.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult. It had great difficulty and almost every other exchange student I talked to had the same experience. I only got accommodation a week before my planned arrival. Recommendation would be to start looking for accommodation as SOON as you feel any certainty that you are going to your destination. Look for any possibilities of accommodation through the university but ALSO privately. This is of course very hard as you don't get much information about the process of finding accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That this will probably what you end up doing as an exchange student (atleast where I went to) and that you should start looking for accommodation independently EARLY (earlier than you think). Living off campus is good because you also get to experience the rest of the city, but living close is better. Most university students do, so socialising is easier when you live close. I lived very close to the university but technically off-campus. I would recommend living as close to the university as possible as this is both the cheapest and easiest.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was none available to single semester exchange students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Overall it was fine. You had to seek the information independently and I also ended up paying for a language assessment test that wasn't needed as this wasn't clear. But if you seek information by e-mail they are happy to help.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had guides but mostly you had to email to get the information that applied specifically to you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not succesful. I applied for 3 different courses, but as I was not informed that I didn't get 2 of those courses, I didn't know that I had to apply for two new courses and how. Instead I just wasn't registered. I quickly had to write and call just to get registered for any course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have the registration done as early as possible and just write the visiting team with anything you are uncertain of, because you are not going to get that information anywhere else.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses (in the assessment) at my host/receiving institution were lower than at UCPH. This could be a bit confusing to accommodate to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They were very different. Not much theory was discussed in my classes at the host-institution. It seems that at my host institution, the teaching was very focused on active participation and discussion in smaller groups of people. At UCPH we mostly have lectures, but I know that they try to incorporate discussions although this can be difficult when you are more than 100 students. At UCPH we have classes of smaller groups of people to discuss the lectures, but it seems that these classes are removed to save money although they are very useful, especially to discuss theory.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 3 courses of 10 ECTS credits each. Migration, Settlement and Belonging. Ways of Living: Studying different worlds. Sociology of Cognition.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Ways of Living as it was different from the courses at UCPH. The two others discussed themes I had already had mostly covered back home. I didn't get to choose the courses myself.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, both eating out and groceries, are a bit cheaper. Housing is veery expensive and difficult to find.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every kind you can think of! There are so many opportunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the community choir as it was very casual and I didn't have to commit for a whole year. It was great, also socially!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I really liked the guided weekend trip I did to Isle of Skye. But go to the highlands! It is beautiful and you can go by train but I would stay for a night. There's also one-day hiking trails closer to the city which is great to do on a weekend, but go early as it gets dark early.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as their way of living is pretty close to what I am used to in Denmark. They are very polite and open.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was difficult, but talk to them in class and most importantly, join a club! Also, living with someone local could also be a great way to meet other locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None were challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very down-to-earth and open to other people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Be aware of the possibilities of housing as soon as possible when applying for the exchange. 2. Don't get too attached to getting specific courses as you probably won't get the ones you want. They are all great and you are going to learn something useful anyway. 3. Say yes to everything social, especially in the beginning of your stay. You are probably going to have a nice time even though it can feel overwhelming. But also; respect your own boundaries - you don't have to be friends with everyone.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You probably will mostly be with other exchange students, so try and meet people from other nationalities than you own! Also, a plus about going somewhere not too far from Denmark is, that you are able to easily go back and visit in years to come and see the city again! It also meant that my friends and family from Denmark could visit me during the weekends. It was great to share my new city with them.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendship I got with my roommate. Also, the experiences in Scottish nature were amazing so make sure to get them even though you feel busy.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely finding accommodation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
